title: The files to open, in boot order

steps.title: A reading list that follows the boot
steps.body:
Each coloured band is one stage of the boot, in the same order as the boot-chain diagram, with the real files behind it. Left column: the stage; middle: the path; right: what the file is for.

Paths are relative to `build/work/Linux_for_Tegra/` after `./build.sh fetch rootfs kernel`. A file marked binary is shipped compiled by NVIDIA, so there is nothing to read in it.

steps.title: For MB1, read the config, not the binary
steps.body:
`bootloader/mb1_t234_prod.bin` is MB1 itself, signed and encrypted by NVIDIA. What you can read is its configuration: the pinmux file `tegra234-mb1-bct-pinmux-p3767-dp-a03.dtsi` is a device tree source for the module.

`flash_t234_qspi.xml` says which firmware image goes into which QSPI-NOR partition and how large it is. Change a pin function or a partition size here and you must reflash the firmware.

steps.title: The board .conf tells the flash tool what this board is
steps.body:
`jetson-orin-nano-devkit-super.conf` is the board definition: it picks the device tree (`DTB_FILE`), the BPMP dtb, the pinmux and the layouts. `p3767.conf.common` holds settings shared by every P3767 module (Orin Nano and Orin NX).

`flash.sh` and `tools/kernel_flash/l4t_initrd_flash.sh` are the drivers that turn the partition XML plus the `.conf` into signed images and flash them.

steps.title: UEFI is configured by files you can open
steps.body:
`mb2_t234.bin` and `uefi_jetson.bin` are shipped as binaries, though the UEFI source is public at github.com/NVIDIA/edk2-nvidia.

UEFI's settings, such as the boot mode and boot device order, arrive as device-tree overlays: `L4TConfiguration.dtbo` and `BootOrder*.dtbo`. L4TLauncher is `BOOTAA64.efi`, and `extlinux.conf` is copied into the root filesystem's `/boot/extlinux/`.

steps.title: The secure OS ships as an image, with sources alongside
steps.body:
The secure OS is OP-TEE, a small trusted operating system that runs apart from Linux. Its image is `bootloader/tos-optee_t234.img`, and `SOURCE.tos-optee_t234.img` names the sources it came from.

Those sources are the tarballs `atf_src.tbz2` and `nvidia-jetson-optee-source.tbz2`, which unpack to `arm-trusted-firmware/` and `optee/optee_os/`.

steps.title: The kernel has a recipe, a config and out-of-tree modules
steps.body:
`source/kernel/Makefile` is NVIDIA's own build recipe (defconfig, Image, dtbs, modules), which `./build.sh kernel` unrolls into visible steps. The configuration is the arm64 `defconfig` of Linux 5.15.148 with the `-tegra` local version.

The out-of-tree modules (GPU, display, camera, hardware performance) live in `nvidia-oot/`, `nvgpu/`, `nvdisplay/` and `hwpm/`, built separately from the kernel tree.

steps.title: The device tree is layered, from board down to module
steps.body:
A device tree describes the hardware to the kernel. The Orin Nano Super devkit file `...-nv-super.dts` includes the `-nv.dts` and trims the CPU OPP table (the allowed frequency and voltage points).

Below it sit the nodes shared by every module on this carrier (aliases, I2S, DMIC, thermal, camera) and the carrier (P3768) and module (P3767) layers. `generic-dts/Makefile` shows how the `.dts` files become `kernel/dtb/*.dtb`.

steps.title: Two scripts build the userland around the sample rootfs
steps.body:
`apply_binaries.sh` and `nv_tegra/nv-apply-debs.sh` install NVIDIA's Debian packages and tarballs into `rootfs/`.

`tools/l4t_create_default_user.sh` creates the login account, and `tools/l4t_update_initrd.sh` rebuilds the initrd, which must match the modules.

steps.title: Search the tree instead of memorizing it
steps.body:
The footer gives three searches: `grep -rn "p3767"` over the board `.conf` files, `grep -rn "MAXN_SUPER"` over `source/hardware/`, and `dtc -I dtb -O dts kernel/dtb/L4TConfiguration.dtbo` to read a compiled overlay as text.

Each file on the page is explained, with what to change and where, in `docs/15-source-tour.md`.
